title: Parallel Courses III
hints: a course can't start until every one of its prerequisites is fully done - which prerequisite determines when it can actually start, the fastest one or the slowest one?

you need each course's finish time, and a course's finish time depends only on its prerequisites' finish times - so compute them in an order where every prerequisite is finished before you compute its dependents
that's a topological order - process courses in topological order, and for each one, its finish time is its own duration plus the LARGEST finish time among its direct prerequisites
a course with no prerequisites simply finishes at its own duration
the overall answer is the maximum finish time across every course, since the whole plan isn't done until the slowest chain completes
commonMistakes: taking the minimum or the sum of prerequisite finish times instead of the maximum
forgetting a course still takes its own time[i] months in addition to waiting for prerequisites
processing courses in an arbitrary order instead of topological order, computing a dependent's finish time before all of its prerequisites are finalized

content.problemStatement:
There are n courses, labeled 0 to n - 1, and a list of prerequisite pairs `relations`, where each pair `[a, b]` means course a must be fully completed before course b can start. You're also given `time`, where `time[i]` is the number of months it takes to complete course i. You may take any number of courses at the same time, as long as each one's prerequisites are already fully completed, and a course, once started, always takes exactly `time[i]` months to finish.

**Return the minimum number of months needed to complete all n courses.**
constraints: each pair [a, b] has 0 <= a, b < n
the relations are guaranteed to form a DAG (no cycles)
notes: no relations at all - the answer is just the single longest individual course duration
a single course with no relations
a long chain where the answer equals the sum of every course's time along that chain
a course with multiple prerequisites that finish at different times - it must wait for the LATEST one, not the first

sampleTestCases.explanation: courses 0 and 1 start immediately (finishing at month 3 and 2); course 2 needs both done, so it starts at month 3 and finishes at 3 + 5 = 8; course 3 then starts at 8 and finishes at 8 + 4 = 12
with no prerequisites, both courses start immediately and run in parallel, finishing after 1 month
course 3 must wait for the later of its two prerequisites (course 2 finishes at month 4, later than course 1's month 3), so 3 starts at 4 and finishes at 8; course 4 then finishes at 8 + 5 = 13

optimal.pattern: process courses in topological order and compute finish[v] = time[v] + max(finish[u] for every prerequisite u), tracking the overall maximum

bruteForce.approach: recompute the finish time for each course by recursively finding the max finish time of all its prerequisites, without memoization, redoing shared subtrees repeatedly
bruteForce.time: O(V * E) or worse without memoization
